compiled_state.title: [test-verify-session-provenance.sh]: date +%s%N -> Non-portable on older BSD/macOS (works by accident on modern macOS)
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Incident Overview

Line 42 of tests/scripts/test-verify-session-provenance.sh uses 'fname="file_$(date +%s%N).txt"'. The %N (nanoseconds) format specifier is a GNU coreutils extension; BSD date (older macOS, FreeBSD) does not support it. Modern macOS (Big Sur+) may support it depending on installed coreutils.

Currently passes on CI (Linux runner) and on the dev machine (modern macOS), but the test suite would fail in environments where %N is not supported.

## Discovery

Flagged by Per-Story LLM Review on PR #145.

## Suggested Fix

Replace with a portable alternative:
- 'date +%s_$$' — epoch seconds plus PID for uniqueness within a process
- Or 'echo $$_$RANDOM' if PID/random is sufficient

## Severity Justification

Priority 3 — affects test portability but does not impact production code or CI. Easy fix.

## Related
- Surfaced during workflow scenario validation

comments.body: Investigation: code at tests/scripts/test-verify-session-provenance.sh:49-50 already has the portable fallback ('date +%s%N 2>/dev/null' with BSD-detection guard checking for empty or '*N' literal, falling through to '$(date +%s)_${$}_${RANDOM}'). Landed in 281055e877 via PR #160. No new code change required.
